assumption_inventory: One Euclidean Brownian driver and its given filtration.
Distinct coordinates and square-integrable weights measurable at each left endpoint.
One uniform second-moment bound on the weights. T may be zero.

substantive_formula_proof_moves.title: Build a third unit projection
substantive_formula_proof_moves.text: Use the normalized sum of the two orthogonal coordinate vectors.

substantive_formula_proof_moves.title: Polarize the increments
substantive_formula_proof_moves.text: The compensated time terms cancel, leaving the product of the two actual coordinate increments.

substantive_formula_proof_moves.title: Transfer the scalar limits
substantive_formula_proof_moves.text: The three compensated sums are square integrable. The mixed squared expectation is bounded by a fixed linear combination of their squared expectations.

units.missing_bridges_or_natural_math_checks: Distinct coordinates give orthogonality. The compensated time terms cancel exactly. The 3,3/4,3/4 quadratic bound is valid. The same C must bound all weight second moments, and T=0 is allowed.
units.natural_math_defect_status: No substantive defect demonstrated at source-only stage.

assumption_inventory: The finite coordinate set has decidable equality. The point $w$ has Euclidean norm one.

For an analytic interpretation of the Hessian, take a twice continuously differentiable ambient test near $w$. The Lean equality itself is algebraic in the totalized Fréchet derivatives and has no smoothness premise.

substantive_formula_proof_moves.title: Expand the projected arguments
substantive_formula_proof_moves.text: Bilinearity gives two mixed radial terms and one term with two radial arguments for each coordinate.
substantive_formula_proof_moves.formula: D^2 f[p_j,p_j]=D^2 f[e_j,e_j]-w_jD^2 f[e_j,w]-w_jD^2 f[w,e_j]+w_j^2D^2 f[w,w].

substantive_formula_proof_moves.title: Sum the radial contributions
substantive_formula_proof_moves.text: The coordinate expansion of $w$ makes each mixed sum equal to the radial Hessian entry. The unit norm makes the squared-coordinate sum one. The remaining diagonal sum is Mathlib's ambient Laplacian.

units.missing_bridges_or_natural_math_checks: The identity is algebraic in totalized derivatives; no Hessian symmetry or smoothness premise is needed for the formal scalar identity. C2 is contextual for the analytic interpretation.
units.natural_math_defect_status: No substantive defect demonstrated at source-only stage.

assumption_inventory: The positive horizon is T. The sample measure is finite, the filtration satisfies the usual conditions, and the driving standard vector Brownian motion is relative to that filtration and measure.
The finite coordinate rows have progressive product-square-integrable diffusion coefficients. Their drift evaluations at each fixed time t≤T are almost-everywhere strongly measurable.
The drift paths are almost surely continuous and have bounded variation on [0,T].

The compact set K has a selected fallback point k₀. On one event of full measure, the process belongs to K at every time in [0,T]. The test is twice continuously Fréchet differentiable at each point of that range.

substantive_formula_proof_moves.title: Place the paths in the compact range
substantive_formula_proof_moves.text: Clip the time at T and apply the Borel fallback outside K. On the event where the original path stays in K, the resulting K-valued path agrees with it at every dyadic grid point.

substantive_formula_proof_moves.title: Derive the coordinate square-sum limits
substantive_formula_proof_moves.text: At the terminal grid point the inclusive prefix contains all fine cells. The scalar quadratic-variation theorem supplies the limit for each actual coordinate.

substantive_formula_proof_moves.title: Apply the Taylor residual estimate
substantive_formula_proof_moves.text: Apply the existing Euclidean residual theorem using these coordinate limits. Equality of the clipped and original paths on the grids gives the claimed sum.

units.missing_bridges_or_natural_math_checks: One full-measure all-time confinement event is needed to replace the path at every grid point. Coordinate quadratic limits are derived, not assumed. The source now has a correctly escaped almost-sure annotation.
units.natural_math_defect_status: No substantive defect demonstrated at source-only stage.

assumption_inventory: The horizon T is positive and the sample measure is finite. The filtration satisfies the usual conditions and the standard vector Brownian motion is relative to that filtration and measure.
The state and Brownian coordinate types are finite with decidable equality. Each diffusion entry is progressive and square-integrable in the product of sample and horizon time measures.
The compact set K has a selected fallback point k₀. On one event of full measure, the process belongs to K at every time in [0,T].
Each initial coordinate is strongly measurable at time zero. Each drift coordinate is strongly progressive and has almost surely integrable time sections on the horizon.
The scalar test is continuously Fréchet differentiable at each point of K.

substantive_formula_proof_moves.title: Take the weighted stochastic limits
substantive_formula_proof_moves.text: For each coordinate use the progressive bounded derivative weight. Apply the weighted stochastic-sum theorem to each actual completed integral to obtain the progressive L² product integrand.

substantive_formula_proof_moves.title: Take the weighted drift limit
substantive_formula_proof_moves.text: On almost every path, the initialized drift increments are increments of the integrable time primitive. The continuous derivative weight therefore gives the ordinary weighted time-integral limit. Almost-sure convergence implies convergence in measure under the finite sample measure.

substantive_formula_proof_moves.title: Assemble the genuine martingale
substantive_formula_proof_moves.text: Each weighted diffusion entry is a progressive L² integrand. Its completed stochastic integral is a martingale. Add them over the finite coordinate pairs. The sum is zero at time zero for every sample.

substantive_formula_proof_moves.title: Recover the derivative on the actual vectors
substantive_formula_proof_moves.text: The finite limits sum in measure. Expand the derivative on the actual increment in its basis, and move the finite drift sum inside the time integral using bounded weights and integrable drift sections.

units.missing_bridges_or_natural_math_checks: The source separates the stochastic and drift limits. The stochastic weighted integrands are genuine progressive L2 objects. The drift argument uses a.e. pathwise integrability plus continuous weights, then finite-measure transfer from a.s. to in-measure convergence. No uniform drift moment bound is claimed.
units.natural_math_defect_status: No substantive defect demonstrated at source-only stage.

assumption_inventory: Let E and F be real normed vector spaces. Derivatives are real Fréchet derivatives; D²f(x) is viewed as a continuous bilinear map.
E is locally compact, K⊆E is compact, and f is C² at every point of K. The set K may be empty.

substantive_formula_proof_moves.title: Choose a compact neighborhood inside the smooth locus
substantive_formula_proof_moves.text: The C² locus is open. Compactness of K and local compactness of E give a compact closed neighborhood of K contained in that locus.

substantive_formula_proof_moves.title: Use uniform continuity of the Hessian
substantive_formula_proof_moves.text: The Hessian is continuous on this compact neighborhood, so a single distance threshold bounds its oscillation by ε.

substantive_formula_proof_moves.title: Keep every short segment in the neighborhood
substantive_formula_proof_moves.text: Take δ=min(ρ,δ₀). Every x+tv with x∈K, ‖v‖<δ and t∈[0,1] remains in the chosen neighborhood and within δ₀ of x. Apply the preceding segment estimate.

units.missing_bridges_or_natural_math_checks: The radius is chosen after epsilon and is uniform over x in K and all small v. No requirement x+v in K is needed. The prior segment estimate is an explicit prerequisite; empty K is permitted.
units.natural_math_defect_status: No substantive defect demonstrated at source-only stage.

assumption_inventory: The sample space Ω carries a finite measure μ. E is a locally compact real normed space with its Borel measurable structure. K⊆E is compact.
f:E→ℝ is C² at every point of K. Each time evaluation of the K-valued process X is measurable. Its paths are continuous on the specified compact time domain for μ-almost every sample.
T>0, X is defined at all nonnegative times and has almost-sure continuous paths on [0,T]. The dyadic sums of squared increments converge in measure to Q:Ω→ℝ.

substantive_formula_proof_moves.title: Restrict time to the compact interval
substantive_formula_proof_moves.text: Every dyadic time lies in [0,T]. Restrict X to this interval, retaining measurable time slices and almost-sure path continuity.

substantive_formula_proof_moves.title: Verify the mesh hypothesis and apply the grid theorem
substantive_formula_proof_moves.text: Consecutive grid points are exactly T/2ⁿ apart, so their distances tend to zero. All hypotheses of the arbitrary-grid residual theorem now hold.

units.missing_bridges_or_natural_math_checks: The quadratic-sum limit to a real Q remains a premise. The theorem transfers it to residual convergence in measure, without asserting stochastic quadratic variation, an L1 limit, or an a.s. limit.
